G2898.d: diminutive of a derivative of the base of κέρας; a skull ("cranium"):--Calvary, skull.

G2970.d: from κεῖμαι; a carousal (as if letting loose):--revelling, rioting.

G2528.d: from κατά; and ὁπλίζω; to equip fully with armor:--arm.

G2641.d: from κατά and λείπω; to leave down, i.e. behind; by implication, to abandon, have remaining:--forsake, leave, reserve.

G2804.d: of Latin origin; Claudius, the name of two Romans:--Claudius.

G2897.d: probably from the same as ἁρπάζω; properly, a headache (as a seizure of pain) from drunkenness, i.e. (by implication) a debauch (by analogy, a glut):--surfeiting.

G2795.d: from (poetic for , to go); to stir (transitively), literally or figuratively:--(re-)move(-r), way.

G2857.d: apparently feminine plural of kolossos ("colossal"); Colossæ, a place in Asia Minor:--Colosse.

G2675.d: from κατά and a derivative of ἄρτιος; to complete thoroughly, i.e. repair (literally or figuratively) or adjust:--fit, frame, mend, (make) perfect(-ly join together), prepare, restore.

G2501.d: of Hebrew origin (יוֹסֵף); Joseph, the name of seven Israelites:--Joseph.

G2557.d: from κακός and the base of ἔργον; a wrong-doer, i.e. criminal:--evil-doer, malefactor.

G2757.d: from a presumed compound of κενός and φωνή; empty sounding, i.e. fruitless discussion:--vain.

G2762.d: feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of κέρας; something horn-like, i.e. (specially) the apex of a Hebrew letter (figuratively, the least particle):--tittle.

G2562.d: feminine of κάλαμος; a stalk of grain, i.e. (collectively) stubble:--stubble.

G2662.d: from κατά and πατέω; to trample down; figuratively, to reject with disdain:--trample, tread (down, underfoot).

G2698.d: from κατά and τίθημι; to place down, i.e. deposit (literally or figuratively):--do, lay, shew.

G2713.d: from κατά and ἔναντι; directly opposite:--before, over against.

G2690.d: from κατά and στρέφω; to turn upside down, i.e. upset:--overthrow.

G2932.d: a primary verb; to get, i.e. acquire (by any means; own):--obtain, possess, provide, purchase.

G2536.d: of Hebrew origin (קֵינָן); Cainan (i.e. Kenan), the name of two patriarchs:--Cainan.

G2865.d: from a primary (to tend, i.e. take care of); properly, to provide for, i.e. (by implication) to carry off (as if from harm; genitive case obtain):--bring, receive.

G2807.d: from κλείω; a key (as shutting a lock), literally or figuratively:--key.

G2735.d: from a compound of κατά and a derivative of ὀρθός (compare διόρθωσις); something made fully upright, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (specially, good public administration):--very worthy deed.

G2864.d: apparently from the same as κομίζω; the hair of the head (locks, as ornamental, and thus differing from θρίξ; which properly denotes merely the scalp):--hair.

G2679.d: from κατά and σκάπτω; to undermine, i.e. (by implication) destroy:--dig down, ruin.

G2692.d: from καταστρέφω; an overturn ("catastrophe"), i.e. demolition; figuratively, apostasy:--overthrow, subverting.

G2626.d: from κατά and the base of κλύδων; to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by implication) to deluge:--overflow.

G2869.d: from κόπος; to tire, i.e. (figuratively) to relax:--cease.

G2558.d: from a presumed compound of κακός and ἔχω; to maltreat:--which suffer adversity, torment.

G2710.d: from κατά and χράομαι; to overuse, i.e. misuse:--abuse.

G2965.d: a primary word; a dog ("hound") (literally or figuratively):--dog.

G2699.d: from a compound of κατά and (to cut); a cutting down (off), i.e. mutilation (ironically):--concision. Compare ἀποκόπτω.

G2582.d: of foreign origin; Candacè, an Egyptian queen:--Candace.

G2954.d: of uncertain origin; Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean:--Cyprus.

G2697.d: from κατέχω; a holding down, i.e. occupancy:--possession.

G2594.d: from a derivative of κράτος (transposed); to be strong, i.e. (figuratively) steadfast (patient):--endure.

G2559.d: from κακός; to injure; figuratively, to exasperate:--make evil affected, entreat evil, harm, hurt, vex.
